page: Hetzner Cloud ccx23 is a general-purpose virtual server featuring dedicated CPU resources. Powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, the instance provides 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.91 GB per core, alongside 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It operates on the QEMU hypervisor under the x86_64 architecture and does not include any GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile. The server demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded bzip3 decompression scoring in the top 25%. However, multi-core scaling is a notable bottleneck; stress-ng multi-core performance, Geekbench multi-core scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all fall into the bottom 25%. Memory subsystem performance is also mixed, showing average write speeds but weak read-only bandwidth for both small and large blocks. Database operations and Redis SET throughput are similarly positioned in the lower 25% tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ccx23 offers dedicated CPU cores, which prevent resource contention from neighboring tenants, making it a stable option for workloads requiring predictable single-threaded execution. However, the resource density and multi-core performance limitations make it less optimal for highly parallelized tasks, large-scale database hosting, or intensive compilation. It is best utilized for light web serving, single-threaded processing tasks, basic text and image processing, or small-scale development environments that benefit from dedicated CPU allocation without requiring high multi-core throughput.
